title: Deterministic Traffic Mirror Simulator for Private/VPC Deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a deterministic traffic mirror simulator that captures, normalizes, and replays representative customer traffic for Private/VPC/on-prem environments with strict control over randomness and KV/cache state. The goal is to provide reproducible throughput (tokens/sec), track latency SLOs (p95/p99), and surface regressions across runtime and kernel changes. The simulator should run against customer topology snapshots, seedable RNG for tokenization/ordering, and provide automated regression detection with alerting to Console and CI gating hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can ingest a topology snapshot and produce a deterministic, repeatable request stream given the same seed
Captured runs include token-level counts, per-request durations, and KV cache footprints; outputs match against golden traces within a small tolerance
Automatic measurement of tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and memory/GPU utilization per model variant
Regression detector flags SLO breaches or >=10% throughput degradation and creates an alert with a diffed histogram and example traces
Simulator integrates with Console to upload run artifacts and with CI to block merges when regression alerts are raised
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Capture format - protobuf event stream with request metadata, sequence lengths, and optional KV warmup markers
Phase 2: Normalizer - translate customer headers/topology into internal runtime targets and normalize timestamps into inter-arrival distributions
Phase 3: Player - seedable traffic generator that enforces KV/cache priming steps and consistent tokenization mapping
Maintain a small canonical SDK for on-host snapshot collection to avoid depending on customer agents
Expose run parameter overrides: seed, concurrency cap, request pacing multiplier, and kernel selection hints
Store run artifacts in S3-compatible bucket with versioned keys and immutable checksums for golden comparisons
